article.headline: Hamilton rain washout forces Black Caps into desperate fight for series draw
article.summary: Heavy rain at Seddon Park abandoned the third ODI between New Zealand and India, leaving the hosts trailing 2-0 in the series.
article.body:
Not a single ball was bowled in Hamilton as persistent weather forced officials to abandon the third ODI of the series. The washout effectively ended New Zealand’s hopes of an ODI series victory against India, leaving the Black Caps unable to win the remaining two matches after already falling 2-0 behind following losses in Auckland and Wellington. The team now faces the prospect of their first home ODI series defeat since 2019.

This result is significant for the Black Caps, who have successfully defended their home turf by winning 11 consecutive ODI series over the last five years. For local fans who turned out for the sellout event, the abandonment denied any chance of a 40-overs-per-side contest. The loss of points and momentum comes at a difficult time as the squad prepares for upcoming test matches.

The challenge for New Zealand deepens as they enter games four and five without several key starters. Players including Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Henry Nicholls, and Nathan Smith are set to depart the ODI group to begin preparations for the test series in Wellington. Additionally, the side faces setbacks with players like Lockie Ferguson withdrawn due to injury, requiring a roster shuffle that brings in reinforcements like Finn Allen and Nick Kelly.

With only two games remaining, New Zealand must secure wins at Bay Oval to avoid a series loss. Both upcoming fixtures will test the depth of the squad as they look to salvage a 2-2 draw.

article.headline: Singaporeans Secure Final Assurance Package Cash Payouts of Up To $250
article.summary: Approximately 3 million Singaporean adults will receive final Assurance Package cash payouts ranging from $100 to $250 starting December 8.
article.body:
Over a five-year span ending in 2026, eligible Singaporeans will have collected a total of up to $2,250 in cash benefits through the government’s comprehensive support scheme. This December’s distribution marks the final installment of the enhanced Assurance Package, an initiative originally introduced to help households navigate rising living costs and the impact of the goods and services tax rate increases.

The Ministry of Finance confirmed that this disbursement serves as the final round of support under the program, which was bolstered by a $3 billion top-up during the 2023 budget. With total funding reaching $9.6 billion, the package has provided sustained assistance to lower- and middle-income families across the nation since 2022.

Individual payouts are determined by assessable income and property ownership status. Citizens owning no more than one property with an annual income of $39,000 or below qualify for the maximum $250 payment. Those with incomes between $39,001 and $100,000 will receive $150, while individuals earning above $100,000 or owning multiple properties are set to receive $100. Eligibility applies to all Singaporeans aged 21 and older as of 2027.

Recipients can verify their status via the official govbenefits.gov.sg portal using Singpass credentials. Notifications will be dispatched via SMS from the official gov.sg Sender ID, while those without registered mobile numbers will receive physical letters. To ensure an earlier arrival on December 8, eligible recipients must link their NRIC to PayNow by November 24. Those opting for GIRO payments must submit their banking details by November 30 to receive funds by December 17.

news.title: Criminal - Official Teaser Trailer
news.og_title: Criminal - Official Teaser Trailer - IGN
news.og_desc: Check out the teaser trailer for Criminal, an upcoming series featuring an interlocking universe of crime stories based on the multi-Eisner Award-winning graphic novel series created by Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips’ bestselling graphic novel series of the same name. Criminal stars Charlie Hunnam, Adria Arjona, Luke Evans, Emilia Clarke, Richard Jenkins, Kadeem Hardison, Gus Halper, John Hawkes, and Logan Browning. The recurring and guest cast includes Michael Mando, Garrett Hedlund, Patrick J. Adams, Pat Healy, Taylor Selé, Aliyah Camacho, Marvin Jones III, Michael Xavier, Dominic Burgess, Chris Diamantopoulos, Lawrence Kao, Katie Stevens, John Pyper-Ferguson, Robert Lee Hart, Aina Brei'yon and Kyle Davis.Criminal begins with the story of two friends, Leo Patterson (Charlie Hunnam) and Ricky Lawless (Gus Halper), one trying to fight his way out of the world of crime they were raised in, the other desperate to follow in the footsteps of his father, a legendary outlaw. And when Ricky's older brother Tracy (Luke Evans) returns home from the Army, their tragic family history comes home with him. Drawn into their orbit are Greta (Adria Arjona), a sharp-tongued car thief from Leo’s past, and Mallory (Emilia Clarke), Ricky's girlfriend, who fears what he'll do to get by. Gunfights, heists, and tragic romance are the order of the day, but will anyone make it out alive?Criminal is based on the graphic novels by Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips, and executive produced by Brubaker, Phillips, Philipp A. Barnett, Anna Boden, Ryan Fleck, Jordan Harper, Sarah Carbiener, Dee Rees, and Halley Gross, along with co-executive producers Cortney Norris and Minhal Baig. It is produced by Amazon MGM Studios, Basement Gang, Inc., Big Indie Pictures, Inc., Gowanus Projections, Inc., and Legendary Television Productions, Inc.All four episodes of Criminal Part One “Coward” will debut on January 13, 2027, followed by all four episodes of Criminal Part Two “Lawless” on January 27, 2027 on Prime Video.
